**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Economics 2 (0525), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: You are required to answer ANY FIVE questions. ONLY THE FIRST FIVE QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED. All the questions carry equal marks. Calculators are allowed.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Aucun écart constaté entre les points imprimés.

Découpage : les sous-parties (i), (ii)... restent dans le texte de la sous-question (a), (b) ou (c) ; quand le sujet imprime des points pour (b)(i) et (b)(ii) séparément, la sous-question « b » porte la somme (ex. 6 + 6 = 12).

Sujet scanné (filigrane gcerevision.com / Kawlo en travers des pages, sans conséquence sur la lisibilité) ; aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Form 5. Les chiffres des exemples (FCFA, indices, ratios) sont hypothétiques et ont été recalculés avec Python ; aucune statistique réelle n'est avancée.

Le sujet tient en quatre pages (page de garde + trois pages de questions) ; aucune question n'est coupée ni illisible. Aucun graphique imprimé dans le sujet : `figures` vide (aucune figure produite pour les corrigés).

Q8(a)(ii) : l'exemple chiffré (1 000 000 d'habitants dont 400 000 enfants, 560 000 en âge de travailler, 40 000 âgés ; ratio de dépendance 78,6) est hypothétique et recalculé avec Python ; aucune statistique réelle du Cameroun n'est avancée (la qualification « population jeune » reste qualitative).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Distinguish between the following:

(i) Youthful and aging population. (4 marks)
(ii) Dependency ratio and working population. (4 marks)
(iii) Immigration and emigration. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Youthful population and ageing population.**

- A **youthful population** has a **large proportion of young people** (usually under 15 years), because of high birth rates and falling infant mortality but relatively short life expectancy. Its population pyramid has a broad base. Many developing countries, Cameroon included, have a youthful population; it brings a heavy demand for schools and child health services and a large future labour force.
- An **ageing population** has a **large and rising proportion of old people** (usually 60 or 65 years and over), because of low birth rates and long life expectancy. Its pyramid has a narrow base and a wide top. It brings a heavy demand for pensions and health care for the elderly and a shortage of young workers.

**(ii) Dependency ratio and working population.**

- The **working population** (labour force) is the part of the population of working age (for example 15 to 64 years) which is **able and willing to work**, whether employed or looking for a job. It produces the goods and services and pays most of the taxes.
- The **dependency ratio** is the **ratio of the dependants** (young people below working age and old people above it) **to the working-age population**:

$$
\text{Dependency ratio}=\frac{\text{number of young dependants}+\text{number of old dependants}}{\text{working-age population}}\times 100
$$

Example (hypothetical): in a population of 1,000,000 with 400,000 children, 560,000 people of working age and 40,000 old people, the dependency ratio is $\frac{400\,000+40\,000}{560\,000}\times100\approx78.6$ dependants for every 100 workers. The working population is thus a number of people, whereas the dependency ratio is a measure of the burden each worker carries.

**(iii) Immigration and emigration.**

- **Immigration** is the **movement of people into a country from other countries** to settle there (for example foreign workers or refugees entering Cameroon). It increases the population of the receiving country.
- **Emigration** is the **movement of people out of a country to settle in another country** (for example skilled Cameroonians leaving to work abroad). It reduces the population of the country of origin and may cause a loss of skilled labour (brain drain).

The difference between the two is *net migration* (immigration minus emigration).

questions.enonce_markdown: State and explain FOUR (4) reasons for the rapid decline in infant mortality rates in our Country. (8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The infant mortality rate is the **number of deaths of children under one year of age per 1,000 live births** in a year. It falls when mothers and babies are healthier and better protected. The following reasons are usually given for the decline.

1. **Improved health services.** More hospitals, health centres and maternity clinics, with more trained doctors, nurses and midwives, mean that pregnant women get prenatal care and safe delivery, and sick babies are treated early.
2. **Immunisation and disease control.** Free or cheap vaccination campaigns against childhood diseases such as measles, polio and tuberculosis, together with malaria control (mosquito nets, spraying), prevent many infant deaths.
3. **Safe water and better sanitation.** Clean drinking water, latrines and waste disposal reduce water-borne diseases such as diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid, which are major killers of babies.
4. **Education of mothers and better nutrition.** Greater literacy and health education teach mothers about breastfeeding, balanced feeding, hygiene and the spacing of births, and higher incomes improve food supply, so that babies are healthier and less likely to die.

**Conclusion.** Government policy, aid programmes and the rise in household incomes and education together explain the fall; it still requires continued investment in health and in the poorest areas.
